title: Bjarne Stroustrup and 'C with Classes' (1979-1983)
explainer: C++ didn't start as a new language - Bjarne Stroustrup began at Bell Labs in 1979 by writing a preprocessor, Cpre, that translated C code extended with Simula-style classes back into plain C so existing compilers could build it. That lineage explains why C++ still feels like 'C plus a type system for objects' rather than a clean-slate design: classes, constructors, and access control were literally bolted onto C syntax before the language was renamed C++ in 1983. Knowing this helps explain why so much of C++'s complexity comes from reconciling C's low-level model with features borrowed from Simula.
